---
title: "crbcc"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    df_print: kable
params:
  csv: "results.csv"
  ## If this value is not empty, the report writes two files for the README
  ## of crbcc to this directory: the figure closures-time-by-size.png and the
  ## shields.io badge speedup.json.
  assets: ""
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, dev = "png", dpi = 120)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
glue <- glue::glue

## The categorical slots 1-2 of the dataviz reference palette, in a fixed order.
COL   <- c(gnur = "#2a78d6", crbcc = "#eb6834")
INK   <- "#0b0b0b"  # primary text
INK2  <- "#52514e"  # secondary text, axes
GRID  <- "#e4e3df"  # grid lines
RANGE <- "#c3c2b7"  # line between the compilers in a dot plot
COMPILERS <- names(COL)

## These lists are the same as in crbcc_bench.py.
BASE <- c("base", "compiler", "graphics", "grDevices", "grid", "methods",
          "parallel", "splines", "stats", "stats4", "tools", "utils")
RECOMMENDED <- c("MASS", "lattice", "Matrix", "nlme", "survival", "boot",
                 "class", "cluster", "codetools", "foreign", "KernSmooth",
                 "mgcv", "nnet", "rpart", "spatial")

## The compilers of each suite. The -fn suites have no compiler column.
SUITES <- list(closures = COMPILERS, `closures-fn` = "",
               install = COMPILERS, `install-fn` = "")

fmt   <- function(x, digits = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
pct   <- function(x) paste0(fmt(100 * x, 0), "%")
times <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(fmt(x, digits), "x")
## Returns "1 run" or "2 runs".
count <- function(n, noun) paste(n, if (n == 1) noun else paste0(noun, "s"))
gmean <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]; exp(mean(log(x))) }
group_of <- function(p) case_when(p %in% BASE ~ "base", p %in% RECOMMENDED ~ "recommended",
                                  TRUE ~ "CRAN")
## Writes markdown with {} expressions. Inline `r` code does not work in asis chunks.
md <- function(...) cat(glue(..., .envir = parent.frame()), "\n\n", sep = "")
## Returns the path of a file in params$assets. If params$assets is empty, returns NULL.
asset <- function(name) {
  if (!nzchar(params$assets)) return(NULL)
  dir.create(params$assets, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  file.path(params$assets, name)
}

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(
  text = element_text(colour = INK2),
  axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2),
  axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK),
  legend.text = element_text(colour = INK),
  strip.text = element_text(colour = INK, hjust = 0, size = 11),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = INK2),
  legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", legend.title = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)))
compiler_fill   <- scale_fill_manual(values = COL, breaks = COMPILERS)
compiler_colour <- scale_colour_manual(values = COL, breaks = COMPILERS)
log_x <- function(...) scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma(), ...)
log_y <- function(...) scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma(), ...)

# Read the report ---------------------------------------------------------

lines <- readLines(params$csv)
meta  <- sub("^# ", "", grep("^#", lines, value = TRUE))
raw   <- read.csv(text = grep("^#", lines, value = TRUE, invert = TRUE),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
if (!"fn" %in% names(raw)) raw$fn <- NA
if (!"compiler" %in% names(raw)) raw$compiler <- NA  # Only -fn suites.
raw <- raw |>
  filter(suite %in% names(SUITES)) |>
  mutate(failure  = ifelse(is.na(failure), "", as.character(failure)),
         compiler = ifelse(is.na(compiler), "", as.character(compiler)),
         fn       = as.character(fn),
         part     = sub("-.*", "", suite))  # closures or install
present <- intersect(names(SUITES), unique(raw$suite))
if (length(present) == 0) stop("The report has no samples of the crbcc_bench.py suites.")

## A run with a failure and no samples has no row in the CSV. The expected
## runs of a suite are the packages of its part, for each compiler of the suite.
expected <- bind_rows(lapply(present, function(s)
  expand_grid(suite = s, benchmark = unique(raw$benchmark[raw$part == sub("-.*", "", s)]),
              compiler = SUITES[[s]])))
failed <- bind_rows(
  raw |> filter(failure != "") |> distinct(suite, benchmark, compiler, failure),
  expected |>
    anti_join(distinct(raw, suite, benchmark, compiler), by = c("suite", "benchmark", "compiler")) |>
    mutate(failure = "no samples in the CSV"))

## The analysis does not use a package that has a run with a failure in the
## same part.
d <- raw |>
  filter(failure == "", !(warmup %in% c("True", TRUE))) |>
  anti_join(failed |> distinct(part = sub("-.*", "", suite), benchmark), by = c("part", "benchmark"))
has <- function(s) any(d$suite == s)

## Returns the median of the runs, with one row for each package and
## compiler. A run can write more than one sample of a metric, one for each R
## process of R CMD INSTALL. Then the value of the run is the sum of its
## samples.
pkg_metric <- function(s, m, f = median) d |>
  filter(suite == s, metric == m) |>
  group_by(benchmark, compiler, run) |> summarise(value = sum(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(benchmark, compiler) |> summarise(value = f(value), .groups = "drop")

## Returns the same values, with one column for each compiler and one row
## for each package in pkgs. A missing value is 0, because a package without
## src/ has no 'native' samples.
pkg_wide <- function(s, m, pkgs, f = median)
  expand_grid(benchmark = pkgs, compiler = COMPILERS) |>
  left_join(pkg_metric(s, m, f), by = c("benchmark", "compiler")) |>
  mutate(value = coalesce(value, 0)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = compiler, values_from = value)

## Returns the packages of a suite, in the order of the GNU R time. The
## longest time is first.
pkg_order <- function(s, m) pkg_metric(s, m) |>
  filter(compiler == "gnur") |> arrange(desc(value)) |> pull(benchmark)

## Returns one row for each closure of a -fn suite: the package, the closure,
## the size, and the time of one compilation (s) for each compiler.
fn_table <- function(s, pkgs) d |>
  filter(suite == s, benchmark %in% pkgs) |>
  select(benchmark, fn, metric, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = value) |>
  transmute(benchmark, fn, size, gnur = time_gnur, crbcc = time_crbcc) |>
  filter(!is.na(gnur), !is.na(crbcc))

## Makes a dot plot of x (benchmark, compiler, value), with the packages in
## the order of pkgs.
dotplot <- function(x, pkgs, xlab) {
  x <- mutate(x, benchmark = factor(benchmark, rev(pkgs)))
  ggplot(x, aes(value, benchmark)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = benchmark), colour = RANGE, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = compiler), shape = 21, colour = "white", size = 3.2, stroke = 0.8) +
    compiler_fill + log_x() + labs(x = xlab, y = NULL)
}

# Function size -----------------------------------------------------------

## Size classes in AST nodes, by powers of 10.
SIZE_BREAKS <- c(1, 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, Inf)
SIZE_LABELS <- c("1-9", "10-99", "100-999", "1,000-9,999", ">= 10,000")
size_class  <- function(size) cut(size, SIZE_BREAKS, SIZE_LABELS, right = FALSE)

## Returns the median time of each compiler and the geometric mean of the
## speedups for each size class.
size_table <- function(fx) fx |>
  group_by(`size (AST nodes)` = size_class(size)) |>
  summarise(closures = fmt(n(), 0),
            `gnur (us)` = fmt(median(gnur) * 1e6),
            `crbcc (us)` = fmt(median(crbcc) * 1e6),
            `gnur / crbcc` = times(gmean(gnur / crbcc)))

size_time_plot <- function(fx) {
  long <- fx |>
    pivot_longer(all_of(COMPILERS), names_to = "compiler", values_to = "time") |>
    mutate(compiler = factor(compiler, COMPILERS))
  mid <- long |>
    group_by(compiler, class = size_class(size)) |>
    summarise(size = median(size), time = median(time), .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(long, aes(size, time * 1e6, colour = compiler)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.4, stroke = 0) +
    geom_line(data = mid, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(data = mid, aes(fill = compiler), shape = 21, colour = "white",
               size = 3, stroke = 0.8) +
    compiler_colour + compiler_fill + log_x() + log_y() +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
    labs(x = "closure size (AST nodes, log scale)", y = "time of one compilation (us, log scale)",
         subtitle = "The points are closures. The line is the median of the size class.")
}

size_speedup_plot <- function(fx) {
  x <- fx |> mutate(speedup = gnur / crbcc) |> filter(is.finite(speedup), speedup > 0)
  mid <- x |>
    group_by(class = size_class(size)) |>
    summarise(size = median(size), speedup = gmean(speedup), .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(x, aes(size, speedup)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.45, stroke = 0, colour = COL[["crbcc"]]) +
    geom_line(data = mid, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(data = mid, colour = INK, size = 2.5) +
    log_x() + log_y() +
    labs(x = "closure size (AST nodes, log scale)", y = "speedup, gnur / crbcc (log scale)",
         subtitle = "The points are closures. The line is the geometric mean of the size class.")
}

size_by_package <- function(fx, pkgs) fx |>
  group_by(package = benchmark) |>
  summarise(closures = fmt(n(), 0), `median size` = fmt(median(size), 0),
            largest = fmt(max(size), 0),
            `gnur / crbcc total` = times(sum(gnur) / sum(crbcc)),
            `gnur / crbcc geo. mean` = times(gmean(gnur / crbcc))) |>
  arrange(match(package, pkgs))

# Closures ----------------------------------------------------------------

## The chunk option fig.height uses pkgs and ipkgs, also if eval is FALSE.
pkgs <- ipkgs <- character()

has_closures <- has("closures")
has_fn       <- has("closures-fn")
if (has_closures || has_fn)
  pkgs <- if (has_closures) pkg_order("closures", "compile") else unique(d$benchmark[d$suite == "closures-fn"])
if (has_closures) {
  time <- pkg_wide("closures", "compile", pkgs) |> mutate(across(all_of(COMPILERS), ~ .x * 1000))
  heap <- pkg_wide("closures", "heap", pkgs)
  rss  <- pkg_wide("closures", "max_rss", pkgs) |> mutate(across(all_of(COMPILERS), ~ .x / 1024))
  tot  <- colSums(time[COMPILERS])
  runs <- d |> filter(suite == "closures") |> group_by(compiler) |> summarise(n = n_distinct(run))
}
if (has_fn) fx <- fn_table("closures-fn", pkgs)

# Install -----------------------------------------------------------------

has_install <- has("install")
has_ifn     <- has("install-fn")
if (has_install || has_ifn)
  ipkgs <- if (has_install) pkg_order("install", "elapsed") else unique(d$benchmark[d$suite == "install-fn"])
if (has_install) {
  elapsed  <- pkg_wide("install", "elapsed", ipkgs)
  bytecode <- pkg_wide("install", "bytecode", ipkgs)
  native   <- pkg_wide("install", "native", ipkgs)
  itot     <- colSums(elapsed[COMPILERS])
  itot_bc  <- colSums(bytecode[COMPILERS])
  iruns <- d |> filter(suite == "install") |> group_by(compiler) |> summarise(n = n_distinct(run))
}
if (has_ifn) ifx <- fn_table("install-fn", ipkgs)
```

```{r parts, include = FALSE}
## Show a part if the CSV has one of its suites, also if all its runs have a
## failure.
part_closures <- any(c("closures", "closures-fn") %in% present)
part_install  <- any(c("install", "install-fn") %in% present)

## Writes the correctness of a part: the closures that are the same as GNU R,
## and the runs with a failure.
correctness <- function(part) {
  s <- paste0(part, "-fn")
  if (s %in% present) {
    ok <- d |> filter(suite == s, metric == "size")
    n  <- n_distinct(expected$benchmark[expected$suite == s])
    md("The suite `{s}` has no failure for {n_distinct(ok$benchmark)} of {count(n, 'package')}. ",
       "The results of {fmt(nrow(ok), 0)} closures are the same as GNU R.")
  } else
    md("The report has no samples of the suite `{s}`.")
  f <- failed |> filter(sub("-.*", "", suite) == part)
  if (nrow(f) > 0) {
    md("**Runs with a failure.** The results do not include the packages that ",
       "have a run with a failure in this part.")
    print(knitr::kable(f, row.names = FALSE))
  }
}

## Writes the packages of a part, and the number of runs of its timed suite.
part_input <- function(p, s, r) {
  if (length(p) == 0) return(invisible())
  groups <- paste(sprintf("%d %s", table(group_of(p)), names(table(group_of(p)))),
                  collapse = ", ")
  md("Packages: {count(length(p), 'package')} ({groups}).")
  if (!is.null(r))
    md("The suite `{s}` has {count(max(r$n), 'run')} for each package and compiler.")
}
```

crbcc compiles R code to byte code. It gives the same byte code as the
compiler package of GNU R, but it is faster.

- [README and source code](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/crbcc#readme)
- [Use crbcc](https://prl-prg.github.io/crbcc/crbcc.html): compile closures
  and install packages with crbcc
- [crbcc on CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=crbcc)

# Benchmarks

```{r summary, results = "asis"}
n_same <- sum(d$suite %in% c("closures-fn", "install-fn") & d$metric == "size")
items <- c(
  if (has_closures)
    glue("**Closures:** crbcc compiles all closures of {count(length(pkgs), 'package')} ",
         "{times(tot['gnur'] / tot['crbcc'])} faster than GNU R."),
  if (has_install)
    glue("**Installation:** with crbcc, R CMD INSTALL of {count(length(ipkgs), 'package')} ",
         "is {times(itot['gnur'] / itot['crbcc'], 2)} faster."),
  if (n_same > 0)
    glue("**Correctness:** the byte code of {fmt(n_same, 0)} closures is the same ",
         "as the byte code of GNU R."))
cat(paste0("- ", items, "\n"), "\n", sep = "")
```

```{asis, echo = TRUE}
The benchmarks compare two compilers: `gnur` (`compiler::cmpfun` of GNU R)
and `crbcc` (`crbcc::cmpfun`). The size of a closure is the number of AST
nodes of its body and of the default values of its formals
(`crbcc:::function_size`). The time of one compilation of a closure
(`crbcc:::compile_time`) is the median time of a batch of compilations,
divided by the number of compilations in the batch. A batch takes a minimum
of 100 us. The speedup of a group of closures is the geometric mean of the
speedups of the closures.

The tables and figures show the median of the runs.
```

```{asis, echo = part_closures}
## Closures

### Methodology

The suites `closures` and `closures-fn` compile the R code of all closures
of a package namespace, not the byte code of the installed package.

- `closures` measures the time and the memory to compile all closures of a
  package. Each compiler has a new R process.
- `closures-fn` compiles each closure with the two compilers in one R
  process. It measures the time of one compilation of the closure. It also
  compares the results with `crbcc:::identical_strict` (`identical()` with
  all strict flags, as `tests/compare.R`). If the results of a closure are
  different, the run is a failure.
```

```{r closures-input, results = "asis", eval = part_closures}
part_input(pkgs, "closures", if (has_closures) runs)
```

```{asis, echo = part_closures}
### Results

#### Correctness
```

```{r closures-correctness, results = "asis", eval = part_closures}

```

```{asis, echo = has_closures}
#### Compile time

The suite `closures` measures the time to compile all closures of a
package.
```

```{r closures-summary, eval = has_closures}
tibble(
  compiler = COMPILERS,
  `compile (s)` = fmt(tot / 1000, 2),
  `vs gnur` = times(tot["gnur"] / tot),
  `heap median (MB)` = fmt(sapply(heap[COMPILERS], median)),
  `heap max (MB)` = fmt(sapply(heap[COMPILERS], max)),
  `RSS median (MB)` = fmt(sapply(rss[COMPILERS], median)),
  `RSS max (MB)` = fmt(sapply(rss[COMPILERS], max)))
```

```{r closures-summary-text, results = "asis", eval = has_closures}
md("`crbcc` needs {fmt(tot['crbcc'] / 1000, 2)} s and `gnur` needs ",
   "{fmt(tot['gnur'] / 1000, 1)} s. In total, `crbcc` is ",
   "{times(tot['gnur'] / tot['crbcc'])} faster.")
if (!is.null(f <- asset("speedup.json")))
  writeLines(sprintf('{"schemaVersion": 1, "label": "compile speedup", "message": "%s faster than GNU R", "color": "blue"}',
                     times(tot["gnur"] / tot["crbcc"])), f)
```

```{r closures-time-plot, eval = has_closures, fig.height = 1.5 + 0.3 * length(pkgs)}
time |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(COMPILERS), names_to = "compiler") |>
  dotplot(pkgs, "compile time of all closures (ms, log scale)")
```

```{r closures-time-table, eval = has_closures}
spread <- function(k) {
  w <- function(f) pkg_wide("closures", "compile", pkgs, f)[[k]]
  (w(max) - w(min)) / w(median)
}
tibble(package = pkgs, group = group_of(pkgs),
       `gnur (ms)` = fmt(time$gnur),
       `crbcc (ms)` = fmt(time$crbcc, 2),
       `gnur / crbcc` = times(time$gnur / time$crbcc),
       `gnur spread` = pct(spread("gnur")),
       `crbcc spread` = pct(spread("crbcc")))
```

```{asis, echo = has_closures}
The column "spread" is (max - min) / median of the runs of the compiler.

#### Memory

- **heap**: the maximum R heap during the compilation, minus the heap
  before it. The value comes from `gc()` "max used" (Ncells + Vcells). R
  records this value at the start of each garbage collection. Thus it
  includes garbage that R did not collect yet. For a compiler that makes
  much garbage, the value is near the GC trigger, not near the live data.
- **RSS**: the maximum resident set size of the R process. It includes R,
  the loaded packages and the compiler.

crbcc keeps its work buffers on the `R_alloc` stack. When `cmpfun` returns,
these buffers become garbage. Thus a high heap value of crbcc shows when R
collects the garbage, not how much live data crbcc has.
```

```{r memory-plot, eval = has_closures, fig.height = 1.5 + 0.3 * length(pkgs)}
bind_rows(heap |> mutate(metric = "maximum R heap during the compilation (MB)"),
          rss |> mutate(metric = "maximum RSS of the R process (MB)")) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(COMPILERS), names_to = "compiler") |>
  dotplot(pkgs, "MB (log scale)") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x")
```

```{r memory-table, eval = has_closures}
tibble(package = pkgs,
       `heap gnur (MB)` = fmt(heap$gnur), `heap crbcc (MB)` = fmt(heap$crbcc),
       `RSS gnur (MB)` = fmt(rss$gnur), `RSS crbcc (MB)` = fmt(rss$crbcc))
```

```{asis, echo = part_install}
## Installation

### Methodology

The suites `install` and `install-fn` install each package from its source
with `R CMD INSTALL`. The hook `inst/r-cmd-install-hook.R` (`R_PROFILE_USER`)
replaces `compiler:::tryCmpfun`, the function that R uses to compile each
closure of the package.

- `install` runs `R CMD INSTALL` one time for each compiler. It measures
  these values:
  - **elapsed**: the wall time of `R CMD INSTALL`.
  - **bytecode**: the time in the byte-code compiler, for all closures of
    the package.
  - **native**: the time to compile and link `src/`. For a package without
    `src/`, the value is 0.
- `install-fn` runs `R CMD INSTALL` one time. It compiles each closure that
  R compiles during the installation with the two compilers, as
  `closures-fn` does. These closures include the S4 methods.
```

```{r install-input, results = "asis", eval = part_install}
part_input(ipkgs, "install", if (has_install) iruns)
```

```{asis, echo = part_install}
### Results

#### Correctness
```

```{r install-correctness, results = "asis", eval = part_install}
correctness("install")
```

```{asis, echo = has_install}
#### Installation time
```

```{r install-summary, eval = has_install}
tibble(compiler = COMPILERS,
       `elapsed (s)` = fmt(itot, 1),
       `vs gnur` = times(itot["gnur"] / itot, 2),
       `bytecode (s)` = fmt(itot_bc, 2),
       `bytecode vs gnur` = times(itot_bc["gnur"] / itot_bc),
       `native (s)` = fmt(colSums(native[COMPILERS]), 1),
       `bytecode share` = pct(itot_bc / itot))
```

```{r install-summary-text, results = "asis", eval = has_install}
md("With `crbcc`, the installation of all packages is {times(itot['gnur'] / itot['crbcc'], 2)} ",
   "faster than with GNU R ({fmt(itot['crbcc'], 1)} s, not {fmt(itot['gnur'], 1)} s). ",
   "The byte-code compilation is {pct(itot_bc['gnur'] / itot['gnur'])} of the installation ",
   "time with GNU R and {pct(itot_bc['crbcc'] / itot['crbcc'])} with `crbcc`. The other ",
   "time of R CMD INSTALL is the same for the two compilers. In this time, R parses the ",
   "code, makes the lazy-load database and the help pages, and loads the package to test it.")
```

```{r install-time-plot, eval = has_install, fig.height = 1.5 + 0.3 * length(ipkgs)}
m <- c("elapsed time of R CMD INSTALL (s)", "byte-code compile time (s)")
bind_rows(elapsed |> mutate(metric = m[1]), bytecode |> mutate(metric = m[2])) |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, m)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(COMPILERS), names_to = "compiler") |>
  dotplot(ipkgs, "s (log scale)") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x")
```

```{r install-time-table, eval = has_install}
tibble(package = ipkgs, group = group_of(ipkgs),
       `gnur (s)` = fmt(elapsed$gnur, 2),
       `crbcc (s)` = fmt(elapsed$crbcc, 2),
       `gnur / crbcc` = times(elapsed$gnur / elapsed$crbcc, 2),
       `bytecode gnur (s)` = fmt(bytecode$gnur, 2),
       `bytecode crbcc (s)` = fmt(bytecode$crbcc, 3),
       `bytecode gnur / crbcc` = times(bytecode$gnur / bytecode$crbcc),
       `native (s)` = fmt(native$gnur, 2),
       `bytecode share gnur` = pct(bytecode$gnur / elapsed$gnur))
```

```{asis, echo = has_install && has_ifn}
#### Package size

The figure shows the byte-code compile time of each package (suite
`install`). The x axis is the sum of the sizes of the closures that R
compiles during the installation (suite `install-fn`).
```

```{r package-size-plot, eval = has_install && has_ifn, fig.height = 4.5}
pz <- bytecode |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(COMPILERS), names_to = "compiler") |>
  inner_join(ifx |> group_by(benchmark) |> summarise(size = sum(size)), by = "benchmark") |>
  mutate(compiler = factor(compiler, COMPILERS))
ggplot(pz, aes(size, value)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = benchmark), colour = RANGE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = compiler), shape = 21, colour = "white", size = 3.5, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = filter(pz, compiler == "gnur"), aes(label = benchmark),
            hjust = -0.2, colour = INK, size = 3.2, check_overlap = TRUE) +
  compiler_fill + log_x(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) + log_y() +
  labs(x = "sum of the sizes of the closures (AST nodes, log scale)",
       y = "byte-code compile time (s, log scale)")
```

```{asis, echo = has_ifn}
#### Function size

The time of one compilation of each closure that R compiles during the
installation (suite `install-fn`), by the size of the closure.
```

```{r ifn-intro, results = "asis", eval = has_ifn}
md("There are {fmt(nrow(ifx), 0)} closures. The median size is {fmt(median(ifx$size), 0)} ",
   "nodes, and the largest closure has {fmt(max(ifx$size), 0)} nodes.")
```

```{asis, echo = has_ifn}
##### By package

The column "total" is the sum of the times of the closures with `gnur`,
```


# Reproduce

```{asis, echo = TRUE}
## Input

The report reads the `--csv` report of
`inst/benchmarks/crbcc_bench.py`. The docstring of `crbcc_bench.py` gives
the columns, the suites and the metrics. If the CSV does not have the
suites of a part, the report does not show that part.

| Part | Suite | Metrics |
|---|---|---|
| Closures | `closures` | `compile`, `heap`, `max_rss` |
| Closures | `closures-fn` | `size`, `time_gnur`, `time_crbcc`, correctness |
| Installation | `install` | `elapsed`, `bytecode`, `native` |
| Installation | `install-fn` | `size`, `time_gnur`, `time_crbcc`, correctness |

To make this report again, run these commands in a work directory that has
the crbcc source in `crbcc/`:

    mkdir -p pkg-lib
    R CMD INSTALL --library=pkg-lib crbcc
    crbcc/inst/benchmarks/crbcc_bench.py --r "$(which R)" --csv results.csv
    Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("crbcc/inst/benchmarks/crbcc_bench.Rmd",
                                  output_dir = ".", knit_root_dir = getwd())'

For more packages, use `--packages`. For the options, use `--help`.
```

```{asis, echo = length(meta) > 0}
## Environment
```

```{r env, eval = length(meta) > 0}
kv <- regmatches(meta, regexpr(": ", meta), invert = TRUE)
tibble(key = vapply(kv, `[`, "", 1),
       value = vapply(kv, function(x) paste(x[-1], collapse = ": "), ""))
```
